note: Relabel only, per the report's primary fix: the breakfast burrito is a documented Santa Fe / New Mexican invention, not a Mexican dish. Dish is internally coherent (no phantom oil, no unused ingredients) so ingredients, spices and steps are untouched.

steps: Cut the corn tortillas into triangles and fry them in a little of the vegetable oil until crisp and golden, or bake them for the lighter version.
Toast the guajillo chile in a dry pan until fragrant, soak it in hot water for ten minutes, then blend it with the tomato, half the onion, the garlic powder, cayenne and cumin.
Fry the blended salsa in the remaining vegetable oil over medium-high heat until it darkens and thickens, about eight minutes, then season with salt and black pepper.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan to your liking.
Fold the tortilla chips into the sauce only seconds before serving so they keep their bite.
Plate the sauced chips and top with the fried eggs, thin slivers of the remaining raw white onion, sliced avocado and crumbled queso fresco.
Thin the Greek yogurt with a splash of water and drizzle it over as a stand-in for Mexican crema.

note: Salsa rebuilt as a real salsa roja: Tomato Sauce -> fresh Tomato, added toasted Guajillo Chile plus Cayenne (standing in for the unavailable Chile de Arbol) and Garlic Powder, and the salsa is now fried before the chips go in. Feta Cheese 25g -> Queso Fresco 30g. Added Vegetable Oil 6g (phantom-oil bug: steps fried chips and salsa with no fat listed) and Greek Yogurt 25g as the in-registry crema stand-in. Chips now folded in at the last second. Roughly +18% cal.

steps: Lightly fry the corn tortillas in a little of the vegetable oil, about twenty seconds per side, until golden with slightly crisp edges.
Mash the black beans into refried beans with a splash of their liquid and a pinch of salt.
Fry the chopped onion, garlic powder and minced serrano chile in the remaining oil, add the tomato sauce, and simmer until it darkens and thickens into a salsa ranchera, about ten minutes.
Season the salsa with salt and black pepper.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the same pan.
Layer the fried tortillas with the refried beans, set the eggs on top and spoon the salsa ranchera over.
Finish with sliced avocado and crumbled queso fresco.

note: 'Rancheros' IS the salsa, so the salsa is now real: added Onion 25g and spice-override Serrano Chile plus Garlic Powder, and the sauce is fried and simmered rather than warmed. Cumin dropped entirely (salsa ranchera has none). Feta Cheese 20g -> Queso Fresco 25g. Tortillas now lightly fried, not dry-warmed, and the beans are mashed into refried beans. Added Vegetable Oil 8g (phantom-oil bug: 'lightly oiled pan' with no fat listed). Roughly +20% cal.

steps: Season the pork shoulder generously with salt, black pepper, cumin and Mexican oregano.
Cook it gently in a heavy pot, submerged in its own rendered fat, with the garlic powder, bay leaves and the juice and peel of the orange, at a bare simmer for about three hours until fork-tender.
Shred the pork with two forks.
Spread the shredded pork out in a hot dry pan or under a broiler until the edges caramelise and crisp - this is what makes it carnitas rather than braised pork.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for thirty seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the crisped pork and finely chopped white onion and cilantro.
Squeeze the lime over the tacos and serve.

note: Pork Loin 150g -> Pork Shoulder 150g (Phase A added the registry row; loin is the leanest cut and cannot crisp, which the report called disqualifying). Orange 30g added, retiring the phantom orange juice in the old step 2. Coleslaw Mix 40g removed (Baja/US convention, and redundant with onion and cilantro). Steps rewritten as confit-then-crisp with the caramelising step that was missing. Oregano -> Mexican Oregano, Cumin 2g -> 1g, added Bay Leaves and Garlic Powder. Macros move as predicted: about +70 cal and -12g protein; no longer a lean high-protein option.

steps: Season the shrimp with salt, black pepper, garlic powder and paprika.
Sear the shrimp in a hot pan with the vegetable oil for one to two minutes per side, until just pink and opaque - shrimp overcook fast.
Whisk the Greek yogurt with the chipotle powder and a squeeze of lime into a chipotle crema.
Shred the cabbage thinly and toss it with the sliced red onion, chopped cilantro, lime juice, Mexican oregano and salt into a dressed slaw.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan.
Lay the shrimp on the tortillas first, spoon the chipotle crema over, then top with the slaw and sliced avocado - sauce straight onto a corn tortilla tears it.
Serve with the remaining lime wedges.

note: Fixed the cabbage-on-cabbage bug: Coleslaw Mix 40g removed, Cabbage raised 60g -> 80g. Added the defining chipotle crema using Greek Yogurt 30g (the report's lean route - Mayonnaise 12g would have pushed the recipe past +25% cal and diluted the high-protein tag). Chipotle Powder substitutes for the unavailable Chipotle in Adobo. Added Red Onion 15g and Cilantro 5g so the slaw is a dressed slaw. Cumin dropped for the Baja profile of garlic powder, paprika and Mexican oregano. Sear time corrected 2-3 min to 1-2 min per side. Added Vegetable Oil 6g (phantom-oil bug: 'hot oiled pan').

steps: Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat with the diced onion, breaking the meat apart as it cooks.
Add the diced potato and chopped tomato with a splash of water, just enough to keep the pan from catching.
Simmer for twelve to fifteen minutes until the potato is tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Season lightly with cumin, Mexican oregano, garlic powder, cayenne, salt and black pepper.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for thirty seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the picadillo and top with chopped cilantro and sliced avocado.

note: Rebuilt as picadillo per the report, which also resolves the near-duplication with Lean Beef Tacos. BBQ Sauce 15g removed (the single most out-of-place ingredient in the slice) and Corn 40g removed (US southwest convention). Added Tomato 80g and Potato 60g, the carne molida con papas base. Renamed off 'Beef Tacos' so the two ground-beef entries are no longer near-identically named. Taco-packet spicing dropped: Chili Powder and Paprika out, Cumin 2g -> 1g, added Garlic Powder, Mexican Oregano and Cayenne (substituting for the unavailable Chile de Arbol). Calories essentially neutral.

steps: Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat with the diced onion, breaking it apart, for six to eight minutes.
Season with cumin, guajillo chile, Mexican oregano, garlic powder, salt and black pepper.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for thirty seconds per side.
Chop the cilantro finely.
Fill the tortillas with the seasoned beef, onion and cilantro.
Squeeze the lime over the tacos and serve with a salsa alongside - Mexican tacos are dressed at the table.

note: Light touch, as the report advised: the corn tortilla / onion / cilantro / lime construction is already the correct street-taco garnish set and is untouched. Ingredient list deliberately left alone (the optional Tomato 60g was skipped so this stands as the plain taco de carne molida now that Beef Tacos has become picadillo). Chili Powder 2g (the US compound blend) replaced with Guajillo Chile 3g, the report's own named alternative to the unavailable Chile de Arbol. Cumin 2g -> 1g, added Garlic Powder and Mexican Oregano. Beef now browns with the onion instead of being dry-rubbed. Macros unchanged.

steps: Rub the duck leg with salt, black pepper, Mexican oregano, garlic powder and a squeeze of the lime, then let it rest for thirty minutes.
Slow-cook the duck leg submerged in its own rendered fat at 90C / 195F for two to three hours until it shreds easily.
Shred the meat with two forks, discarding the bones, then crisp the skin separately in a hot dry pan until it snaps like chicharron and crumble it over the meat.
Spread the shredded duck out in the hot pan and let the edges caramelise.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for thirty seconds per side.
Mash the avocado with the minced serrano chile and lime juice into a loose salsa.
Fill each tortilla with the duck, finely chopped white onion and cilantro, spoon the avocado salsa over and squeeze more lime on top.

note: Renamed off the French term to Tacos de Pato, the real Mexican dish (duck carnitas). Duck Leg 120g and the 90C confit are correct and kept. Coleslaw Mix 40g removed for finely chopped white Onion 30g; Avocado 40g added for the salsa (tomatillo would be ideal but is not in the registry, so this is the avocado-lime-serrano version Bayless serves). Smoked Paprika (Spanish pimenton) and Cumin both removed - neither appears in any documented version - for Mexican Oregano, Garlic Powder and Serrano Chile, the Bayless direction the report recommended. Steps now crisp the skin like chicharron instead of discarding it, and caramelise the shredded meat. About +67 cal, protein unchanged.

_summary.notes: All 8 recipes changed. Breakfast Burrito is a pure cuisine relabel (Mexican -> American, New Mexican origin) with no other field touched - report's primary fix, not the alternative rebuild. Two renames: Beef Tacos -> Tacos de Picadillo, Duck Confit Tacos -> Tacos de Pato; merge keys on originalName. Four phantom-cooking-oil bugs fixed by adding Vegetable Oil (Chilaquiles 6g, Huevos Rancheros 8g, Shrimp Tacos 6g); one phantom-ingredient bug fixed by adding Orange 30g to Carnitas. No Water was ever added to an ingredients array. ORPHAN WATCH for the merge: Coleslaw Mix is now dropped from all three recipes in this slice that used it (Carnitas, Shrimp, Duck) and is a strong registry-orphan candidate - sweep the other slices before deleting. BBQ Sauce and Corn dropped from Beef Tacos, Pork Loin dropped from Carnitas, Chili Powder dropped from both beef tacos, Feta Cheese dropped from Chilaquiles and Huevos Rancheros (still used by Mediterranean recipes, do not delete), Smoked Paprika dropped from Duck only. MEAT_INGREDIENTS: Pork Shoulder is newly referenced by this slice - confirm it is in the Set. Largest macro move is Carnitas (~+70 cal, ~-12g protein from loin -> shoulder), exactly as the report predicted; every recipe stayed within +/-25% of its original calories. No nuts, no olives, no sumac anywhere.
